fixes.explanation: Ha, the writer never warns anybody about sharing in the rest too soon. He says to be careful that none of them be deemed to have fallen short of the rest (Hebrews 4:1). Getting there too soon is a worry I'd love to have, honestly. The real concern is falling short of the promise.

True, baker. The writer says God has spoken somewhere about the seventh day, and he quotes it: “And on the seventh day God rested from all His works.” (Hebrews 4:4) So he really does point back to creation, just like the card says.

Not false, friend. The writer says God has spoken somewhere about the seventh day, and he quotes it: “And on the seventh day God rested from all His works.” (Hebrews 4:4) So he really does point back to the seventh day. The text says God rested from all His works.

You've got it, baker. The writer says, "For if Joshua had given them rest, God would not have spoken later about another day." (Hebrews 4:8) God did speak later about another day. So the rest the writer means wasn't already given by Joshua.

Work, that's the word. The writer says, "For whoever enters God’s rest also rests from his own work, just as God did from His." (Hebrews 4:10) The pattern is God's own rest. He rested from His works, and whoever enters His rest rests from his own.
